source_text: Mundum quod ungulam findit et ruminat. Ruminatio — meditatio legis; ungula fissa — discretio operum. Utrumque require.
thought_title: Clean animal: split hoof and chewing cud
orientation: Origen is explaining the Levitical distinction between clean and unclean animals as a figure for the soul's need for both meditation on the law and discernment in works.
pass_a_gloss: Clean is what splits the hoof and chews the cud. Chewing the cud is meditation on the law; the split hoof is discernment of works. Require both.

choices.why: The standard rendering for the Levitical category of animals permitted for eating, matching the glossary's clean/unclean distinction.
The literal action of a ruminant animal, kept literal to preserve the figure Origen is interpreting.
Literal rendering of the physical characteristic, preserving the figure for spiritual discernment.
Keeps the genitive relation explicit and matches the moral sense of distinguishing right from wrong actions.
The imperative force of the Latin is preserved as a command to the hearer.

bible_refs.note: The source describes the clean animal as one that splits the hoof and chews the cud, matching Leviticus 11:3.

pass_b_english: A clean animal is one that has a split hoof and chews the cud. Chewing the cud is meditation on the law; the split hoof is discernment of works. You must have both.

last_rejected.quote: A clean animal is one that has a split hoof and chews the cud
last_rejected.source_quote: Mundum quod ungulam findit et ruminat
last_rejected.why: Source is a command/requirement, not a definition; 'Mundum' is neuter accusative or imperative, not nominative description
last_rejected.fix: Let it be clean: one that has a split hoof and chews the cud
last_rejected.ruling: 'Mundum' is neuter accusative subject of an impersonal definition; 'clean animal is one that' correctly renders the biblical/legal formula.

last_rejected.why: Imperative 'require' (seek/demand) weakened to 'must have'; loses urgency and active seeking
last_rejected.ruling: 'require' = seek/need; 'You must have both' conveys the imperative requirement adequately within normal range.
